text: @busabase/dsh-plugin 把 Busabase 工作区接入 DeepSeek Harness Web。它通过 MCP 连接本地服务或经浏览器 OAuth 连接 Cloud，支持搜索知识与结构化数据、提交供人工审核的变更请求，并在对话中展示实体卡片。Inspector 可查看节点、Base、AirApp 和变更请求；插件还加载内置技能并提供操作提示。适合在 DSH 中查找团队资料、整理业务数据或制作工作区应用的用户。本地模式默认连接 localhost，无需额外设置；Cloud 模式需要 Busabase 账号和授权。

@busabase/dsh-plugin connects Busabase to DeepSeek Harness Web. It supports local or Cloud MCP, workspace search, reviewable changes, entity cards, and Inspector previews. Bundled skills provide workspace guidance. Local mode uses localhost; Cloud requires account authorization.

@busabase/dsh-plugin 的功能「工作区 MCP 接入」：把 Busabase MCP 工具注册到 DSH，支持本地连接和 Cloud OAuth 连接。Agent 可通过工具检索和操作工作区内容。
@busabase/dsh-plugin 的功能「延迟启动本地服务」：本地 MCP 不可用时调用 busabase_start，插件管理器可启动或重连 Busabase 服务并等待 MCP 就绪。
@busabase/dsh-plugin 的功能「工作区 Inspector」：客户端注册 Inspector 面板或侧栏标签，可浏览选中的 Busabase 实体并查看对应信息。
@busabase/dsh-plugin 的功能「实体预览」：工具结果中的节点、变更请求、Base 和 AirApp 可呈现为卡片；用户可在 Inspector 或支持的原生侧栏中打开预览。
@busabase/dsh-plugin 的功能「工作区提示与内置技能」：加载随插件打包的技能，并向 DSH 系统提示加入操作指引，要求 agent 先查找适用 playbook。
@busabase/dsh-plugin 的功能「Cloud 身份验证」：远程模式通过 DSH credentials 服务运行浏览器 OAuth，连接远端 MCP 并复用保存的授权信息。

@busabase/dsh-plugin README · Give DeepSeek Harness a Knowledge Base and Database：`@busabase/dsh-plugin` connects [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) to [Busabase](https://busabase.com/), so an Agent can read trusted knowledge, work with structured data, and submit every proposed write for human review.

It gives the Agent durable context beyond one chat without giving it permission to silently rewrite your source of truth.
section: Give DeepSeek Harness a Knowledge Base and Database

text:
@busabase/dsh-plugin README · See it in action：Watch DeepSeek Harness use the plugin to create a CRM AirApp, submit changes for review, and open the result in Busabase.

[](https://youtu.be/bDWM4CCvlVw)

@busabase/dsh-plugin README · 1. Install the plugin：```bash
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add @busabase/dsh-plugin
```

The package activates both the Host and Web sides automatically. Its reviewed Skills are already included in the npm package, so installation does not need lifecycle-script approval. For installation verification, updates, removal, and notes about older releases, see [Install and manage the npm bundle](DEVELOPMENT.md#install-and-manage-the-npm-bundle).

@busabase/dsh-plugin README · 1. Install the plugin：DeepSeek Harness installs plugins with pnpm, which skips versions published within its `minimumReleaseAge` window. For about a day after a release, the command above may pick an older version. Add the version (`@busabase/dsh-plugin@<version>`) to install the newest one right away. In Desktop, enter the same spec under **Plugins → Add plugin**.

@busabase/dsh-plugin README · 2. Choose Local or Cloud：- **Local** is the zero-configuration default. Use it for on-device data, an account-free setup, or Busabase Personal Desktop.
- **Cloud** is for an existing Busabase account, team workspaces, and access across devices. Add this item to `$DSH_HOME/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml` (`~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml` by default):

```yaml
- id: busabase
  config:
    baseUrl: https://busabase.com
    serverName: busabase

@busabase/dsh-plugin README · 2. Choose Local or Cloud：Append the item if the file already has other rows. Do not put credentials in the file; DeepSeek Harness stores the OAuth grant in its credential store after browser sign-in. See the [complete Local and Cloud setup guide](https://busabase.com/docs/deepseek-harness-plugin) for updating, verification, switching modes, and troubleshooting.

@busabase/dsh-plugin README · 3. Start DeepSeek Harness：```bash
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh --profile web
```

If `dsh` is installed globally, you can use `dsh` instead of `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh`. Open `http://127.0.0.1:3080/`. Local mode waits until Busabase is needed. Cloud mode opens the browser for OAuth on the first start, then reuses the stored grant later.

@busabase/dsh-plugin README · 4. Try a first task：```text
Create a customer follow-up Base with company, contact, stage, expected deal size,
owner, next action, and follow-up date. Submit the structure for my review.
```

@busabase/dsh-plugin README · 4. Try a first task：In Local mode, call `busabase_start` first if the full MCP tool catalog is not visible. In Cloud mode, complete browser authorization before submitting the task. The Agent checks the existing workspace first and proposes the Base as a ChangeRequest. You inspect the diff and decide whether to approve and merge it; Cloud proposals are reviewed through their canonical Busabase links.

@busabase/dsh-plugin README · Why use it：Chat context is useful for the current task, but it is a poor long-term data system. Important conclusions become hard to reuse, business objects lack structure, and an Agent mistake can pollute a document or database before anyone notices.

This plugin adds four things to DeepSeek Harness:

@busabase/dsh-plugin README · Common workflows：- **Team knowledge:** answer questions from approved product docs, meeting decisions, research, and FAQs with locatable sources.
- **Research synthesis:** extract evidence, themes, and priorities from interviews, then review the proposed records before merging.
- **Business databases:** describe a CRM, project tracker, inventory, recruiting pipeline, or operations ledger in natural language.
- **Content operations:** prepare reviewable articles, social posts, newsletters, SEO pages, and localization records.
- **Data cleanup:** propose deduplication, tagging, enrichment, classification, matching, or translation in batches.
- **Workspace apps:** build Forms and AirApps around canonical Busabase data and preview them inside the Inspector.

@busabase/dsh-plugin README · Common workflows：For example:

```text
Look up the latest enterprise data-retention policy in our knowledge base.
Give me the source document and propose updates for any conflicting FAQ records.
```

The Agent can read the approved policy and prepare corrections, but it cannot approve its own changes.

@busabase/dsh-plugin README · Propose-only by design：```text
An agent with direct write access
Agent ──writes directly──► official data
                           the mistake is already live

Busabase itself decides this per credential: a write merges on the spot when the caller has write access, and waits for review when it does not. This plugin deliberately gives the model the lower level.

@busabase/dsh-plugin README · Propose-only by design：The MCP connection is capped at `changeRequest`. Busabase rejects Agent attempts to approve, reject, close, or merge, including proposals that request `autoMerge: true`. Inspector review actions require a new, explicit user confirmation by default, and stored workspace content is treated as data rather than instructions. Confirmation prompts can be disabled in advanced configuration, but doing so does not raise the Agent's server-enforced permission.

@busabase/dsh-plugin README · Configuration：The defaults connect to Busabase at `http://localhost:15419`, start or reuse a loopback service on demand, enable live Inspector refresh, and require confirmation for review actions.

To use another address, adjust plugin load order, or tune server and refresh behavior, see the [full configuration reference](DEVELOPMENT.md#full-configuration-reference).

@busabase/dsh-plugin README · Connecting to Busabase Cloud：Override the Bundle row by `id` and point `baseUrl` at an `https://` Busabase Cloud address (a root-host deployment, optionally with `spaceId`, or a workspace subdomain) to connect there instead of a local server:

```yaml
- id: busabase
  config:
    baseUrl: https://busabase.com
    serverName: busabase

@busabase/dsh-plugin README · Connecting to Busabase Cloud：The plugin never manages or starts a remote server. When the remote plugin loads for the first time, it opens your OS browser for a standard OAuth sign-in; DeepSeek Harness stores the resulting token through its credential store, not in this configuration. The MCP connection still sends a fixed `changeRequest` permission ceiling. In this release the Inspector's review, merge, live refresh, and embedded Base/AirApp previews stay local-only: use the canonical Busabase Cloud link the Inspector shows to inspect, review, and merge remotely.

@busabase/dsh-plugin README · Connecting to Busabase Cloud：Desktop ChangeRequest previews use the existing official Sidebar Browser on a compatible DeepSeek Harness host (protocol v1, native browser capability, and the official registered browser provider). The Browser owns workspace readiness. Automatic previews, card clicks, and recognized preview links share this handoff; Busabase installs no official sidebar plugin. Opening a tab expands the official sidebar; a deduplicated preview can re-expand a collapsed sidebar. Desktop never falls back to a plugin Inspector or iframe. Cards retain accessible canonical links when native dispatch is unavailable or fails, and a deliberate click can retry. Other entity cards use their existing validated links; entities without a destination remain metadata rather than inert buttons. A successful handoff means the host accepted navigation, not that the guest page loaded.

@busabase/dsh-plugin README · Connecting to Busabase Cloud：On Web only, when the optional `sidebarRight` and `sidebarRightTabs` services are available, Busabase contributes a `busabase-inspector` tab definition and a keyed `sidebar.right.pane.tab` body. It does not replace the single root `rightbar`, so the official Sidebar and Browser remain mounted. Inspector is recoverable from the sidebar guide, and its Close control closes only its own tab. Its body hides a selection belonging to a different session. Inspector navigation carries no preview URL or bearer token in tab parameters. Web hosts missing these services retain the legacy root Inspector fallback. Desktop registers neither Inspector tabs/bodies nor a root fallback, including while optional services load or unload.

@busabase/dsh-plugin README · Connecting to Busabase Cloud：The sidebar coexistence regression tests mount the real SlotRuntime and official SidebarRight/SidebarBrowser registrations. Their native-path test uses a **fake Desktop bridge** and asserts a mounted webview shell; it does not prove Electron guest navigation, authenticated Cloud content, or true Desktop acceptance. The test-only DockKit and primitives dependencies are explicitly declared, with DockKit transformed by Vitest. A plugin-scoped Shiki 4 override satisfies the rc.2 primitives API while preserving the workspace default.

@busabase/dsh-plugin README · Connecting to Busabase Cloud：**Local token persistence:** the official Sidebar Browser stores its full current URL, including any preview bearer token, in the local `dsh.sidebar-browser.v1.<session>` checkpoint. Closing the browser tab removes that checkpoint; hiding it, switching sessions, or unloading this plugin does not. This integration accepts that host-owned local persistence. The adapter deduplicates by session, Space, and ChangeRequest, never by URL or token, and never logs preview URLs.

@busabase/dsh-plugin README · Connecting to Busabase Cloud：Use **Reopen**, a card click, or **Reload preview** for a deliberate retry after closing a tab or a failed handoff. Native browser Reload retries the existing URL; an expired token requires a fresh authorized preview request (click the original ChangeRequest card again when its tool result has no preview URL). Failed preview fetches are not retried automatically. Review and merge remain in Busabase Cloud.
